tagline: Leading supplier of process control and yield management solutions for semiconductor manufacturing
hero_kpi_rationale: Key indicator of profitability and operational efficiency for semiconductor equipment makers, reflecting KLAC's ability to manage its production costs despite pricing pressures and geopolitical challenges
company_description: KLA Corporation, together with its subsidiaries, designs, manufactures, and markets process control, process-enabling, and yield management solutions for the semiconductor and related electronics industries worldwide. The company operates through three segments: Semiconductor Process Control; Specialty Semiconductor Process; and PCB and Component Inspection. It offers inspection and review tools to identify, locate, characterize, review, and analyze defects on various surfaces of patterned and unpatterned wafers; metrology systems to measure pattern dimensions, film thickness, film stress, layer-to-layer alignment, pattern placement, surface topography, and electro-optical properties for wafers; chemical process control equipment; wired and wireless sensor wafers and reticles; wafer defect inspection, review, and metrology systems; reticle inspection and metrology systems; wafer inspection and metrology systems; and semiconductor software solutions that provide run-time process control, defect excursion identification, process corrections, and defect classification to accelerate yield learning rates and reduce production risk. kpis.name: Gross Margin
kpis.description: KLAC's gross margin increased by 0.9 percentage points in 2025 compared to 2024, rising from 60.0% to 60.9%

kpis.name: Net Income
kpis.description: KLAC's net income increased by 47.1% in 2025 compared to 2024, rising from $2,761.9M to $4,061.6M

kpis.name: Services Revenue
kpis.explanation: Proportion of services in total revenue
kpis.description: Services accounted for 22% of KLAC's total revenue in 2025, growing year-on-year driven by an expanding installed base and recurring subscription contracts
kpis.signal: Growing contribution of services to total revenue

kpis.name: Total Revenues
kpis.description: KLAC's total revenue increased by 24.5% in 2025 compared to 2024, rising from $9,812.2M to $12,156.2M

kpis.name: R&D Expense
kpis.explanation: Annual investment in research and development to maintain KLA's technological leadership.
kpis.description: R&D expenses reached $1.36B in FY2025, up 6.4% vs FY2024. They represent approximately 11.2% of total revenue.

kpis.name: Operating Cash Flow
kpis.explanation: Cash generated from core operating activities, a key indicator of underlying profitability.
kpis.description: Operating cash flow reached $4.08B in FY2025, up 23.4% year-on-year, reflecting strong profitability and effective working capital management.

kpis.name: Diluted EPS
kpis.explanation: Net income attributable to KLA divided by the weighted average number of diluted shares, a key measure of per-share value creation.
kpis.description: Diluted EPS surged to $30.37 in FY2025 (+49.8% vs $20.28 in FY2024), driven by strong net income growth and a reduction in shares outstanding through buybacks.

kpis.name: Product Revenue
kpis.explanation: Revenue from equipment and systems sales, excluding services, representing the core of KLA's business.
kpis.description: Product revenue reached $9.47B in FY2025, up 26.6% vs FY2024, recovering from a dip in FY2024. It represents 77.9% of total revenue.

kpis.name: Capital Expenditures
kpis.explanation: Investments in physical assets necessary to maintain and expand KLA's operational capacity.
kpis.description: Capex amounted to $335M in FY2025, up 20.9% vs FY2024, signaling increased industrial capacity. It remains moderate at 2.8% of revenue.

kpis.name: Non-GAAP Diluted EPS
kpis.explanation: Adjusted earnings per share (excluding non-recurring items) to better compare underlying profitability year-on-year.

kpis.name: Free Cash Flow LTM
kpis.explanation: Measures the actual cash generated by KLA over 12 months after capital expenditures. Indicates financial health and ability to pay dividends.

kpis.name: Semiconductor Process Control Rev
kpis.explanation: Revenue from quality control tools for electronic chip manufacturing, measuring demand for inspection.

kpis.name: Capital Returns LTM
kpis.explanation: Measures the amount of capital KLA returns to shareholders via buybacks and dividends over the past 12 months.

kpis.name: R&D % Sales
kpis.explanation: Measures the percentage of sales dedicated to research and development, reflecting KLA's investment in technological innovation.

kpis.name: Dividend per Share
kpis.description: Annual dividend per share paid, aggregated from yfinance.dividends over the last seven fiscal years reported by the company.
kpis.signal: Dividend per share of $1.9 in the latest year.

kpis.name: Capital Returned (Dividends)
kpis.description: Capital returned to shareholders via annual dividends, extracted from yfinance.cashflow over the last four fiscal years reported.
kpis.signal: Capital returned to shareholders via dividends of $0.905B in the latest year.

kpis.name: Payout Ratio
kpis.description: Payout Ratio = Dividends Paid / Net Income, calculated over the last four fiscal years from yfinance.cashflow and yfinance.income_stmt.
kpis.signal: Percentage of net income distributed as dividends: 22.3% in the latest year.

kpis.name: Gross Margin
kpis.description: KLAC's gross margin increased by 0.9 percentage points in 2025 compared to 2024, rising from 60.0% to 60.9%, despite pricing pressures and geopolitical challenges

kpis.name: Services Revenue
kpis.explanation: Proportion of services in total revenue
kpis.description: Services accounted for 22% of KLAC's total revenue in 2025, with quarter-on-quarter growth year-on-year, driven by recurring subscription contracts linked to an expanding installed base
kpis.signal: Growing contribution of services to total revenue

kpis.name: Earnings Per Share
kpis.explanation: Net income divided by the weighted average number of diluted shares during the fiscal year. Measures the company's ability to generate earnings per share — basis for Payout Ratio calculation (DPS / EPS).

risks.title: China Trade Restrictions
risks.summary: Commercial or government measures, particularly between the U.S. and China, could block access to key markets and severely harm revenues. KLAC has already experienced order book reductions and deposit refunds from Chinese customers.
risks.score_rationale: The risk is cited at the beginning of the MD&A as potentially significantly impacting operations, especially in China. The language is strong (significantly impact, adversely affect). The decline in revenue percentage from Chinese customers in 2025 confirms material impact. Increased prominence vs prior year due to rising geopolitical tensions. Geopolitical category heavily weighted. (default score, to be refined)

risks.title: Declining Demand in PCB/Display
risks.summary: Deteriorating outlook in the PCB and display markets is leading to significant asset impairments and threatening the profitability of these segments.
risks.score_rationale: The text mentions massive impairment charges in 2024 and 2025 due to downgraded forecasts for PCB and Display businesses. Language is alarming (continued deterioration, downward revision). Decision to exit the Display market. Direct impact on asset value. (default score, to be refined)

risks.title: Recurring Goodwill Impairment
risks.summary: The carrying value of goodwill is fragile and subject to write-downs if future segment performance fails to meet expectations.
risks.score_rationale: Repeated goodwill impairments ($230M in 2025, $192M in 2024). The text indicates high sensitivity to growth assumptions and discount rates. Risk of further write-downs if forecasts decline. (default score, to be refined)

risks.title: Uncertain Accounting Estimates
risks.summary: Accounting choices, particularly on revenue recognition and inventory valuation, rely on uncertain assumptions that could affect reported results.
risks.score_rationale: The risk covers several critical areas (revenue, inventory, taxes, deferred tax). The text emphasizes the subjective and inherently uncertain nature of judgments. Direct impact on results and margins. (default score, to be refined)

risks.title: Customer and Geographic Concentration
risks.summary: High dependence on a few customers and the Asian region exposes the company to regional or commercial shocks.
risks.score_rationale: Explicit mention of customer concentration and heavy reliance on Asia. The text directly links this to revenue volatility. Risk amplified by geopolitical tensions. Central position in the Results section. (default score, to be refined)

risks.title: Sensitive Internal Restructuring
risks.summary: Changes in the organizational structure of segments may impact performance and trigger accounting losses.
risks.score_rationale: An internal reorganization in 2025 triggered impairment tests. The text links restructuring to changes in reporting units. Risk of operational disruptions or poor integration. (default score, to be refined)

risks.title: Unusable California Tax Credits
risks.summary: California tax credits may never be utilized, resulting in an accounting value loss.
risks.score_rationale: The amount of the provision ($310M) is significant. The text explains that California tax rules prevent future use of the credits. Risk of a dry loss if unresolved. (default score, to be refined)

risks.title: Impact of Tariffs and Protectionist Measures
risks.summary: U.S. tariffs and foreign countermeasures negatively affect operating results, though KLAC has partially offset this through cost management and volume.
risks.score_rationale: The MD&A explicitly states that recent tariffs imposed by the U.S. government had a negative impact on results. Impact described as immaterial in 2025 but with uncertainty on duration and magnitude. Positive outlook expected with cost management. (default score, to be refined)

ai_positioning.summary: KLAC mentions AI and HPC applications indirectly through increased investments in process control for advanced technologies (2-nanometer) and packaging applications for AI and high-performance computing.
evidence: Demand for advanced semiconductor technologies, particularly evident in the 2-nanometer node, which is seeing higher levels of investment and process control intensity, continues to drive investments in AI
Increasing complexity and value of semiconductor packages, particularly for AI and HPC applications, is also driving significant growth in our advanced packaging business
